results.corrected_title: Swedish legal-AI firm Legora raises $550 million Series E at an $8.8 billion valuation
results.corrected_summary: On 21 October 2026 Swedish legal-AI company Legora announced a $550 million Series E led by Atreides Management, at an $8.8 billion valuation. That is up from $5.6 billion earlier in 2026. New investors include Baron Capital, Capital Group, Fidelity Management & Research, Glade Brook Capital Partners and J.P. Morgan. Legora says its annual recurring revenue is above $200 million, and it has more than 1,000 employees in 18 offices.
key_facts: $550M Series E led by Atreides Management, announced 21 Oct 2026
New investors: Baron Capital, Capital Group, Fidelity, Glade Brook, J.P. Morgan
ARR above $200M (TechCrunch: up from $100M in April)
1,000+ employees in 18 offices; 140,000+ legal professionals at 2,400+ law firms and in-house teams in 80+ markets
results.issues: Sources disagree on when the $5.6B valuation was set: Legal IT Insider says March, TechCrunch says an April Series D extension, so the month has been left out. The '140,000 lawyers' figure is actually '140,000+ legal professionals'. Fidelity's full name is Fidelity Management & Research. The Law.com link returned 403 and was not checked.

results.corrected_title: KrF wants a temporary halt to new data centres in Norway until stricter rules are in place
results.corrected_summary: KrF leader Dag-Inge Ulstein wants a temporary halt to new data centres until stricter regulation is in place, and is seeking a Storting majority. A planned site at Sjøholt in Ålesund, about the size of 35 football pitches, is part of the background. KrF voted against a similar Rødt proposal last year but has changed its position. Frp opposes a full halt but wants rules, Høyre calls a halt symbolic but says regulation is urgent, and Ap points to a white paper due toward the end of 2027.
key_facts: NRK Møre og Romsdal, 22 Oct 2026: KrF (Dag-Inge Ulstein) wants a temporary halt to new data centres
Sjøholt site in Ålesund is about 35 football pitches
KrF voted against a similar Rødt proposal last year, now changed position
Frp (Listhaug) wants operating rules and national control of power allocation; Høyre (Stokkebø) calls a halt symbolic; Ap white paper due toward end of 2027
Over 100 data centre projects planned; Teknologirådet: about 90% of Norwegian data centres have foreign owners
NRK Nordland, 23 Oct: Eika and Nordea investment directors warn of a bubble in heavily debt-financed AI data centres (e.g. Nscale)
results.issues: The Teknologirådet figure is 90% of data centres with foreign owners, not 90% of capacity. Frp wants operating rules and national power control; 'binding rules' is a fair paraphrase. The NRK Nordland bubble warning is a separate article about financial risk around Nscale and others, not part of KrF's proposal.

results.corrected_title: OpenAI's models and Codex come to Google Cloud's Model Garden
results.corrected_summary: On 21 October 2026 OpenAI and Google Cloud announced that OpenAI's frontier models and Codex agentic workflows are coming to Google Cloud's Model Garden. Access starts as a private preview for selected enterprise customers, with wider access planned in the coming weeks. Customers can buy through Google Cloud Marketplace and count the usage against existing Google Cloud commitments. OpenAI says the models will soon be in Google Antigravity and Gemini Agent; with AWS since April, OpenAI is now on all three major US clouds.
key_facts: Announced 21 Oct 2026 by OpenAI and Google Cloud
OpenAI frontier models and Codex workflows in Google Cloud Model Garden
Private preview for selected enterprise customers; broader access in coming weeks
Buy via Google Cloud Marketplace; usage can count against existing cloud commitments
Coming soon to Google Antigravity and Gemini Agent
OpenAI models on AWS since April 2026 after Microsoft exclusivity ended; now on all three major clouds
results.issues: The OpenAI post and TechTarget do not mention the private preview, Marketplace or commitments; these come from TechNode Global and other secondary coverage. TechNode refers to 'Gemini for business' rather than Gemini Agent; the OpenAI post says Gemini Agent. Slashdot and Securities.io were not opened. Reported model names (e.g. 'GPT-6 Astra') came from low-authority blogs only and are left out.
